CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman for: security warnings, irreversible action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread, user asks to clarify or repeats question. Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

message.content: <local-command-caveat>Caveat: The messages below were generated by the user while running local commands. DO NOT respond to these messages or otherwise consider them in your response unless the user explicitly asks you to.</local-command-caveat>
<local-command-stdout>Set model to [1mFable 5[22m and saved as your default for new sessions with [1mmedium[22m effort</local-command-stdout>

content: Auto mode lets Claude handle permission prompts automatically — Claude checks each tool call for risky actions and prompt injection before executing. Actions Claude identifies as safe are executed, while actions Claude identifies as risky are blocked and Claude may try a different approach. Ideal for long-running tasks. Sessions are slightly more expensive. Claude can make mistakes that allow harmful commands to run, it's recommended to only use in isolated environments. Shift+Tab to change mode.

<command-name>/goal</command-name>
            <command-message>goal</command-message>
            <command-args>Hey there! Please read agents.md, read all files it wants you to, and follow it word for word. TASK: Build a basic training script for a 1M paramater model, it should be hyper effecent, with paramaters. HOW: read plan.md. DATASET: fineweb-edu with quality limit, only do above 4 for the score.  REQUIREMENTS: Must be hyper optimized for my hardware, never bloat ram, it should be hyper fast and effecent, ect...  You will train the model on the highest of high quality fineweb-edu data for 2B tokens and provide the scores. Notes: it will be a huge codebase, use a huge folder tree to house all of the data.  At the end of every training session it shall do the proper benchmark + SLERP implementation. You will test the entire framework end to end and get a output score.  ALso, please edit agents.md to say that whenvever editing the training script to change something, you MUST run a 2B token test per feature. Do not add two things and test, you dont know what did what. All scores will be placed into scores.md, this will keep track of commit ID + what was done + if its being keeped or not + description.  You will **NOT** kill any running processes, but you will work around them smartly, do not assume the GPU will be the same, it may be in use, it may not have a GPU, it could be a 3060, ect... plan for everything by using smart systems that will auto detect stuff and attempt to get the absolute maximum out of whatever hardware it is given. At no point shall you hardcode a batch size, gradient accumulation size, or tokens. You will never cap the max checkpoitns it can have saved at any given time (Like limiting to 80 checkpoints) it shall save everything with no limits. ALl print statements, saving stuff, or logs may not intriupt the training process on whateever device it may be on at the time. (stalling quickly to update a log is not tolerated). At the start of the training run it will pull down the models + scores from https://huggingface.co/spaces/Glint-Research/Tiny-ML-Leaderboard on Effecency and overall, then find out where it places in both of those and should properly log it. At the end when everything is being benchmarked it shall get the score on the benchmark leaderboard (using  the pre cached scores for this training run) and will show every model benchmarked where it places in both sorting modes, then at the end right before SLERP it will show the best one, during benchmarking SLERP combinations it will do the same flow of showing the place it scores at in both sorting modes. It will do this for every slerp iteration. At the end it will show the user the final placing in the leaderboard along with individual benchmark scores. When logging to the terminal, never use emojis, use a tdqm progress bar (that expects to be re-sized and doesnt bug out) and logs every 2k steps (also when it saves). So, the overall flow will be this. python3 train.py [number of tokens in billions, like 12 for 12B] [quality score limiter, 4 default, only get scores that are above this or matchig it for data quality]. Once that is ran it will asses how its going to train, its going to see what it has avalible, benchmark the system (do not save, assume new system and new conditions every time), it will see the best batch size, trainign configs, ect... then it will begin the training, if it encounters an OOM it will auto decreese batch size by five, then resume. THere will be no cap on how many times it can decreese add gradient accumulation to make up for the lost batch size. Once training is completed it will look in checkpoints, auto benchmark for the best possible benchmarking config, then it will benchmark all checkpoints using that optimial config for speed (number of questions used for benchmarks will not change). Use wikitext-2, BLiMP, and ARC-Easy datasets. Once benchmarking is done it will do multiple combimnations of SLERP on multipe checkpoints, then it will loop until there is one checkpoint remaining, OR until all newly created slerp checkpoints are worse than the previous best in all catagorys. It should optimize for increesing all scores, not just one.   (do not train on SFT for now). Ensure you follow agents.md presicely.</command-args>
